claims.statement: Tom Allen had been a saloon keeper in St. Louis and operated the Sportsmen's Rest at Sixth and Market.
claims.excerpt: He had been a saloon keeper in St. Louis, had operated the Sportsmen’s Rest at Sixth and Market,

claims.statement: Tom Allen defeated Bill McCoole for the championship on Chouteau Island in the Mississippi in September 1871.
claims.excerpt: had defeated Bill McCoole for the championship on Chouteau Island in the Mississippi in September of 1871.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost the championship to Joe Goss in 1876 on a foul.
claims.excerpt: He defended against all. comers until 1876 when he lost the title on a foul to Joe Goss.

claims.statement: Tom Allen returned to his native England for a visit in 1878.
claims.excerpt: Two years later he returned to his native England

claims.statement: Tom Allen was presented with a huge silver cup by his friends and admirers on 22 May 1878.
claims.excerpt: silver cup by his friends and admirers. That happened exactly 100 years ago on next May 22.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost interest in boxing and retired when the Marquis of Queensberry refined the rules of the game.
claims.excerpt: Allen lost interest in boxing when the Marquis of Queensberry, appalled by the bloody carnage he had witnessed in the bare knuckle brawls, refined the rules of the game.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's daughter Mary, also called Polly, came to the United States with him and later married Edward Taylor of St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: States with him and she subsequently married Edward Taylor of St.. Louis.

claims.statement: Edward Taylor and Polly Allen Taylor were the grandparents of Thomas Allen Taylor, Tom Allen's great-grandson.
claims.excerpt: They are the grandparents of Thomas Allen Taylor, chairman of the Board of the Seven Up Company
When Allen died in 1903, it was assumed he left some money.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's will left everything to his daughter Polly Allen Taylor and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove.
claims.excerpt: His will left everything to his daughter, Polly Allen Taylor, and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove.

claims.statement: When Tom Allen's will was probated, the estate was valued at $278.35.
claims.excerpt: had gone the way of fighters up to this day. The will amounted to $278.35.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's silver cup went to Miss Hartgrove, and was retrieved from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938 by Tom Taylor's father.
claims.excerpt: until my father retrieved it from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938

claims.statement: A family story says Tom Allen came into possession of a diamond belt, emblematic of the world championship, but no one can verify it.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen came into possession of a diamond belt, emblematic of the world championship.

claims.statement: Tom Taylor plans to offer Tom Allen's silver cup to the Missouri Historical Society.
claims.excerpt: He plans to offer the silver cup, the lone remaining memento of his great grandfather’s reign as champion, to the Missouri Historical Society.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's saloon was prosperous, selling whiskey to spectators at the island fights.
claims.excerpt: his saloon had been prosperous, he had made a fair amount of money selling whiskey to the spectators who gathered for the fights on the islands.
